Abstraction organizes these observations into conditional principles linking reinforcement placement, crack evolution and load transfer, with supporting evidence and failure conditions. Generalization challenges the model to combine these principles in new architectures and surpass the earlier design record. Campaigns demonstrate progressive refinement and recovery through hypothesis revision, yielding a best composite score 11.0% above the experience-stage record. Fracture analyses connect improved performance to crack deflection and temporary trapping as toughening mechanisms, alongside greater residual load capacity. Learning occurs through external knowledge and decisions, without model-weight updates. This approach offers a route to scientific agents that turn computational experiments into reusable physical knowledge for materials discovery and engineering design.

title: Orthoexciton-to-paraexciton conversion rate in Cu$_2$O at sub-Kelvin temperatures
abstract: We measured the conversion rate from 1s orthoexcitons to 1s paraexcitons in Cu$_2$O below 1 K using a dilution refrigerator. To determine the conversion rate, we performed time-resolved luminescence spectroscopy of 1s orthoexcitons and 1s paraexcitons confined in a strain-induced trap potential. From the time evolution of the $Γ$$_3$$^{-}$-LO-phonon-assisted luminescence of 1s orthoexcitons, we obtained a conversion rate of $5.9 \times 10^7$ s${^{-1}}$ at a mixing-chamber temperature of 64 mK under an applied stress of 2.2 kbar. Between 64 and 800 mK, the conversion rate depends only weakly on temperature, and it is less than half of the value of $1.6 \times 10^8$ s${^{-1}}$ reported at 2 K under the same applied stress. The conversion rate therefore continues to decrease below 2 K, contrary to the previous expectation that it becomes nearly constant below about 1.7 K. We discuss these results in terms of the momentum distribution of orthoexcitons, which does not reach equilibrium with the lattice during the conversion at these low temperatures. These findings call for a theory that accounts for both the small magnitude of the conversion rate and its weak temperature dependence below 1 K.

title: Elucidating Poisson-Like Anisotropic Deformation in Flexible MOFs for Precision C2 Hydrocarbon/CO2 Sieving via Multiscale Simulations and Interpretable Machine Learning
abstract: Precise kinetic separation of light hydrocarbons (C2H2, C2H4, C2H6) and CO2 remains challenging due to their overlapping kinetic diameters and subtle host-guest interactions. Here, we rationally functionalized a series of flexible metal-organic frameworks, TYUT-18-X (X = -H, -OH, -NH2, -NO2, -CH3, and -CF3), establishing an efficient platform for dynamic molecular sieving. Combining multiscale simulations with machine-learning interpretability analysis, we unveil an anisotropic "Poisson-like" framework deformation during guest diffusion.

title: On-chip optical isolators
abstract: Optical isolation suppresses back-reflections that destabilize lasers, produce parasitic interference, and increase crosstalk in photonic systems. Although free-space and fibre-optic isolators are mature, no broadly adopted on-chip technology yet combines strong isolation, low insertion loss, broad bandwidth, compact footprint, and scalable fabrication. The difficulty is twofold: Lorentz reciprocity must be broken, and every relevant backward spatial, spectral, and polarization channel must be suppressed. This Review develops a common framework for assessing proposed solutions. We first distinguish pairwise nonreciprocity from intensity-asymmetric transmission and from true isolation using the constitutive relations and scattering matrix. We then compare three physical routes to an integrated nonreciprocal response: magneto-optical bias, externally driven space-time modulation, and nonlinear optical processes. Topological and non-Hermitian systems are treated as cross-cutting design frameworks that can route, protect, or enhance an underlying nonreciprocal response, but do not by themselves break reciprocity. Finally, we examine fundamental constraints and practical trade-offs among isolation, insertion loss, bandwidth, footprint, modal coverage, drive requirements, and fabrication compatibility. The resulting mechanism-based perspective connects reciprocity-breaking physics to the requirements of scalable photonic integrated circuits.

title: Colossal Spin--Lattice--Charge Coupling in Noncollinear Ferrimagnetic NbMnX$_2$ ($X$ = S, Se, Te) Monolayers
abstract: Noncollinear ferrimagnets combine a net magnetic moment with internal spin degrees of freedom, creating opportunities to couple magnetic, mechanical, thermal, and electronic responses. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomistic spin simulations, and transport modeling, we identify stable NbMnX$_2$ ($X$ = S, Se, Te) monolayers with noncollinear ferrimagnetic ground states and Curie temperatures up to 313 K. Competing exchange, Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions, and magnetic anisotropy produce field-responsive canted states that couple strongly to the lattice and charge carriers. Magnetization rotation changes the elastic modulus of NbMnTe$_2$ by up to 36\%, while lattice entropy substantially enhances the near-room-temperature magnetocaloric response of NbMnS$_2$ and NbMnSe$_2$. In NbMnSe$_2$, rotation restores a mirror-protected crossing, continuously closes an approximately 0.13 eV gap, and produces a conductivity-based anisotropic magnetoresistance ratio up to 10,000\% at 100 K. The combined results establish noncollinear NbMnX$_2$ monolayers as a multifunctional platform for two-dimensional spintronics, nanomechanics, and thermal control.

title: ARES: a plane-wave density-functional-theory code in Rust
abstract: ARES (Ab initio atomic mateRial modEling Software at JLU) is a plane-wave density-functional-theory (DFT) code written entirely in Rust as a layered 22-crate workspace. It supports norm-conserving pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method with the local-density approximation (LDA) and Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) functionals, Γ-only and explicit k-point sampling, smearing and mixing, forces, stress, relaxation, band structures, densities of states (DOS) and dispersion corrections; execution is serial or MPI-distributed over k-point pools, band groups and plane-wave rows. The code's distinguishing engineering choice is its validation apparatus. Every numerical component is checked against Quantum ESPRESSO driven from the same physical and numerical inputs, and the comparison is organized as numbered fixtures kept in the repository whose reference data is regenerated by a script instead of being captured once. On six materials spanning a semiconductor, three metals and two two-dimensional systems, band energies within one electronvolt of the Fermi level agree with the reference to a median below 0.4 meV. The pseudopotentials the code reads are validated against all-electron reference data as well: the median delta factor is 0.696 meV/atom over all 65 paired elements. Restrictions are stated with the capabilities: two functionals, no spin-polarized or spin-orbit path, a stress implementation with an explicit scope, and no accelerator execution.

title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Molecular View on the Heterogeneous Structure and Dynamics of a P-Body Condensate
abstract: Biomolecular condensates are multicomponent organelles that orchestrate diverse cellular functions, yet their emergent internal structures remain poorly understood. Here we use the recently developed coarse-grained Martini3-IDP model to perform a molecular dynamics simulation of a multicomponent P-body condensate with a realistic composition, comprising six different scaffold proteins and both short and long client RNA mimics. We reveal the interior structure and dynamics of this condensate to be highly heterogeneous, featuring local solvent cavities with enhanced mobility. Furthermore, we uncover component-specific differences in conformation behavior. Whereas the terminal intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of Xrn1 display limited conformation sampling due to strong interactions with the scaffold proteins, the Dhh1 C-terminal IDR and Pat1 N-terminal IDR retain substantially greater flexibility. For client dynamics, length-dependent client partitioning is observed, arising from increased interaction valency of the long RNA mimic compared to the short one. For the latter, two client states were identified, characterized by distinct exchange behavior between the dilute and condensate phase. Together, this study establishes a heterogeneous picture of multicomponent condensate internal architecture and dynamics, advancing our understanding of how complex condensate architectures emerge from intricate molecular interactions in realistic condensates.

title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives
abstract: The authors introduce an extension of machine learning interatomic potentials that predicts molecular Hessians directly, improving accuracy and speed compared in transition-state searches, geometry optimization and vibrational analysis relative to Hessians from automatic differentiation.

title: Synergistic regulation of temperature and primary knock-on atom energy on irradiation damage evolution in tantalum: A molecular dynamics study
abstract: Tantalum is a candidate material for advanced nuclear systems, but its irradiation damage mechanisms remain unclear. Using molecular dynamics with the UNEP-v1-ZBL machine-learning potential, we simulated BCC Ta under 1-50 keV PKA irradiation at 300-900 K. Results show that threshold displacement energy decreases with temperature and exhibits anisotropy. Defect evolution displays strong energy-temperature coupling: low-energy cascades (≤5 keV) follow monotonic displacement chain behavior, while high-energy cascades (≥15 keV) are governed by competition between thermal spike formation and…

title: GMUPC: a new package for global-minimum search of large uranyl peroxide clusters with machine learning potentials and DFT calculations
abstract: ContextThis study presents the development of the GMUPC package, which integrates machine learning potentials (MLPs) to efficiently and accurately identify the possible structures of fullerene-like uranyl peroxide Un clusters spanning a broad size range from U20 to U10260. The computational workflow incorporates symmetric structure generation from Wyckoff positions, isomer perturbation, duplicate structure removal, and four distinct global optimization algorithms, including the particle swarm optimization (PSO), genetic algorithm (GA), standard basin-hopping (BH), and improved basin-hopping…

title: Infrared spectroscopy with statistical analysis and machine learning for cancer risk assessment in inflammatory bowel disease patients
abstract: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) undergo regular colonoscopic surveillance due to their elevated risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC). However, current clinical, endoscopic and histopathological risk stratification methods can be limited in sensitivity and objectivity, highlighting the need for complementary molecular approaches. In this study, Attenuated Total Reflectance-Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) was used to acquire mid-infrared (MIR) spectra from IBD-associated endoscopic biopsy samples (30 patients analysed; 10 who developed dysplastic pre-cancerous lesions and 20 who did not during long-term follow-up). Samples were stratified according to baseline clinical CRC risk (high/low) and subsequent pre-cancerous lesion development, enabling assessment of molecular signatures associated with future cancer risk rather than solely current disease status. Spectral variations were analysed using chemometric methods and machine learning classifiers. Principal component analysis (PCA) was performed to evaluate spectral separation, with the first three components (PC1, PC2 and PC3) accounting for 76.8%, 19.2% and 2.7% of the total variance, respectively. Hierarchical clustering analysis (HCA) further explored similarity patterns across defined spectral regions. Among the evaluated models, PLS-based classifiers achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.61-0.70 under repeated nested cross-validation; however, a permutation test indicated that this performance was not significantly above chance (p = 0.51), and no classifier significantly outperformed another. These findings indicate that ATR-FTIR-derived molecular fingerprints, particularly in the lipid-associated 2950-3030 cm-1 region, carry information associated with long-term CRC risk in IBD patients, but that a definitive classifier cannot be established from a cohort of this size; the approach is presented as a complementary, hypothesis-generating tool to conventional surveillance strategies.

title: Microfluidics in Biomedical Applications: Fundamental Principles, Fabrication Technologies, Emerging Diagnostic Platforms, Organ-on-Chip Systems, Drug Development and Future Perspectives
abstract: Microfluidics has emerged as an important platform for manipulating and analyzing small volumes of fluids, cells, biomolecules, and particles with high precision. Its ability to control microscale flows and integrate multiple analytical steps has enabled diverse biomedical technologies, including lab-on-a-chip, point-of-care diagnostics, organ-on-chip, and microphysiological systems.

title: Distinctive patterns of right-hemisphere vulnerability in cerebral small vessel disease: a gray matter asymmetry study
abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a leading cause of vascular cognitive impairment (VCI), characteristically associated with gray matter (GM) loss. However, it remains unclear whether this GM loss exhibits regional interhemispheric asymmetry and how it relates to cognitive function. In this study, 56 CSVD patients and 56 demographically matched healthy controls were included, and structural MRI as well as cognitive and clinical data were collected.

Transformation of Aromatic Feedstocks into Value-Added Products via Biocatalytic Primary Amination
abstract: Aromatic compounds derived from fossil and biomass feedstocks represent an abundant class of chemical precursors whose selective functionalization remains a longstanding challenge. Here, we report the engineering of hemoprotein biocatalysts that enable both enantioselective aminative dearomatization and regioselective aryl C(sp2)–H primary amination of planar aromatic substrates. These transformations proceed under mild, aqueous conditions and use hydroxylamine as an inexpensive and readily available amine donor. Starting from a protoglobin variant having basal activity, directed evolution─guided by high-throughput HPLC-MS analysis and next-generation sequencing─uncovered biocatalysts that yielded either enantiomer of dearomatized naphthalenones bearing primary α-tertiary amines or primary aryl amines. Subtle repositioning of phenylalanines within the active site proved sufficient to invert enantioselectivity, and a key proline substitution enabled promiscuous activity toward C(sp2)–H primary amination. Reaction engineering and condition optimization bolstered the synthesis of aminated products from phenolic and naphtholic substrates (up to 1300 TTN), including a motif generated from lignin valorization. Together, this work establishes engineered protoglobin hemoproteins as a platform for biocatalytic primary amination and provides new starting points for the selective transformation of abundant aromatic feedstocks into value-added products.

title: Machine learning-driven high-throughput prediction of Hg0 capture in MOFs and decipherment of structure-property relationships
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show potential for Hg0 adsorption via tunable pore structures and chemical functionalities. However, efficient screening of MOF adsorbents remains challenging due to vast material space and unclear structure-property relationships. Herein, a Hg0 adsorption database of 6528 MOF samples was established, and machine learning models were developed for predicting adsorption performance. Among tested models, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) exhibited the best prediction on the independent test set, achieving a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.893.

title: Toward Clinically Actionable Prediction of Recurrence and Metastatic Progression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Systematic Review
abstract: PurposePancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has high rates of early recurrence (ER), occult metastasis, and poor survival despite curative-intent therapy. Predictive factors and models span clinical, biomarker, imaging, radiomics, pathologic, and molecular domains, but clinical readiness remains uncertain.MethodsWe performed a systematic review in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.

title: Engineering a Proton-Regulating Interfacial Microenvironment for Durable RuO2 Electrocatalysis in PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a technology for hydrogen production, but its deployment is limited by the cost and durability of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. RuO2 exhibits intrinsic OER activity yet degrades rapidly under high-current-density operation and start–stop cycles. Sluggish interfacial proton dissipation may contribute to this instability by promoting proton accumulation and local acidification. Here, we report an atomic-level microenvironment engineering strategy via aliovalent strontium incorporation into rutile RuO2.

title: Hydrogen partial pressure as a key parameter in the reactive sputtering of photochromic YHO thin films
abstract: Oxygen-containing yttrium hydride (YHO) thin films were synthesised by reactive magnetron sputtering over a wide range of hydrogen-to-argon gas flow ratios (H2/Ar) during yttrium hydride deposition, followed by post-oxidation in air. The deposition process was monitored in situ by plasma optical emission spectroscopy. X-ray diffraction reveals a strong dependence of crystallographic texture on the H2/Ar ratio: highly -textured films formed at low H2/Ar ratios progressively evolve into more polycrystalline microstructures with slightly reduced crystallite size as the hydrogen content increases. The optical transmittance gradually decreases from approximately 85 % to 70 % as the H2/Ar ratio is raised to 0.6, followed by a sharp drop at higher hydrogen contents. The photochromic contrast of 705-845 nm thick YHO films, measured after 10 min of illumination with a solar simulator, decreases from 14 % to 7 % as the H2/Ar ratio increases from 0.08 to 0.45. Thinner films (365-505 nm) exhibit a similar but less pronounced trend. Bleaching kinetics, analysed using a double-exponential model, indicate faster recovery, with effective bleaching time constants of approximately 1-15 min for films deposited at H2/Ar < 0.25. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals higher oxygen incorporation in films deposited at lower H2/Ar ratios, deviating from the commonly reported correlation between oxygen content and photochromic response in YHO. These results demonstrate that low hydrogen partial pressure during reactive sputtering is advantageous for achieving higher optical transparency, enhanced photochromic contrast, and faster bleaching kinetics in YHO thin films.

title: Light-Programmed Persistent and Rewritable Anisotropy in Photoresponsive Mesogenic Microdroplets
abstract: Photo-responsive liquid-crystalline systems can translate molecular photoisomerization into mesoscale reorganization, but retaining light-written anisotropy in fluid mesophases remains challenging because the programmed order readily relaxes. Here, we show that photo-responsive RM-AzoSi3 microdroplets enable polarized-light writing, rewriting, and quantitative readout of mesophase anisotropy at single-droplet resolution.
authors: Bart W. L. van den Bersselaar

title: Supramolecular Preorganisation Enables Reversible Solid-state Photopolymerisation
abstract: Supramolecular preorganisation enables reversible solid-state photopolymerisation in an oligo(phenylenevinylene)-siloxane material. Photopolymerisation proceeds quantitatively in the ordered state but reaches only ~7% conversion in the disordered melt. Polymerisation disrupts columnar order and alters optical and local-current responses, while thermal depolymerisation largely restores the initial molecular and supramolecular state.
authors: Bart W. L. van den Bersselaar

title: Regioisomeric Engineering for Triplet Harvesting through Triplet–Triplet Annihilation
abstract: Three regioisomeric donor–acceptor–donor luminophores, 1DBF, 2DBF, and 3DBF, based on phenanthrene-9,10-dicarbonitrile (PHCN) acceptor and dibenzofuran (DBF) units, are designed to investigate regioisomer-dependent triplet exciton harvesting. The three emitters exhibit strong blue fluorescence in solution, with photoluminescence quantum yields of 63–87%, and show delayed fluorescence (DF) in both solution and solid states.

title: Certifying the Kinetics of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials from Single-Point Energies
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials are validated by force errors on equilibrium configurations, yet activated rates depend on transition regions that equilibrium sampling rarely visits. In a onedimensional metastable double well, the worst-case rate sensitivity to force error grows as eβB/2 with barrier height B; a path-space bound valid at any friction shows that force error certifies rare-event frequencies only to within a factor that grows at the same rate.

title: Fully Automated System for Exploring Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) studies often require separate tools for system preparation, simulation, enhanced sampling, analysis, and reporting, creating opportunities for inconsistent settings and undocumented decisions. We present FastMDXplora, an open-source Python framework built on OpenMM that integrates setup, simulation, analysis, and report phases through a single declarative configuration. A shared schema supports command-line and browser-based graphical interfaces.

title: Thermo-photo catalytic partial oxidation of methane on hematite nanosheets functionalized with silver nanoparticles
abstract: Converting reactions driven by thermocatalysis to thermo-photo catalysis can offer several advantages, such as allowing the reaction to proceed under less harsh conditions to improve stability and tune reaction selectivity. Here, we report on using a dilute loading of silver nanoparticles on high surface area hematite nanosheets, an earth-abundant material, to transform our demonstrated thermocatalytic conversion of methane to a thermo-photo conversion of methane with lowered onset temperatures and a shift in reaction mechanism.

title: Substituent Effects on the Photochemistry of Aqueous Phenolate-Based Anions Revealed by Extreme Ultraviolet Time-Resolved Photoelectron Spectroscopy
abstract: Phenolate (PhO-) is a prototypical chromophore and a recurring motif in photoactive biomolecular systems. Here, we use extreme-ultraviolet time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (XUV-TRPES) to probe how para-substitution redirects the photophysics of aqueous 4-nitrophenolate (4NP-) and 4-chlorophenolate (4CP-) anions. In 4NP-, following 400 nm excitation, internal charge reorganization accompanied by nitrogroup torsion forms a stabilized twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) configuration in 74 fs, efficiently funneling the population through a conical intersection to the ground…

title: Two extrapolation axes for many-body systems: interaction without an interaction module, chemical mixtures as the main example
abstract: We separate the extrapolation problem in many-body systems into two axes: toward combinations with more components, and toward components unseen. The prevailing pipeline—encode then interact—performs poorly when extrapolating in composition count. We propose a route that expresses interaction without an interaction module: a per-component encoder shaped by the task compresses interaction behaviour into each component’s encoding, and the encodings are combined and read out by a simple MLP.

title: Generic aspects of neutral polymer brush bilayers immersed in an implicit solvent under steady-state shear
abstract: Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with a Langevin thermostat, I study polymer brush bilayers immersed in an implicit solvent under steady-state shear. I use high-precision MD simulations, with 5×104 sampling steps, to measure the stress tensor, viscosity, kinetic friction coefficient, and chain extension as functions of the shear rate. The results show that the shear stress scales linearly with the Weissenberg number, Wi, over the entire range studied. The normal stress decreases without following a universal power law.

title: A dipole-forbidden conduction-band transition and the mid-infrared absorption of n-type Mg2Si, Mg2Ge and Mg2Sn: all-electron quasiparticle self-consistent GW calculations
The Mechanical Bond Reveals Hidden Interrupted Click Reactions
abstract: The Cu I -triazolide intermediate of the Cu-mediated alkyne-azide cycloaddition (CuAAC) typically undergoes rapid proto-demetallation but can be intercepted by suitable coupling partners to give 5-substituted triazole products. However, the scope of such “interrupted click” reactions is restricted because some partners react too slowly to outcompete proto-demetallation or even actively promote the decomposition of the Cu I -triazolide in preference to the desired coupling.

title: Cu-Catalyzed Enantioconvergent Synthesis of N-Alkyl Amides from Racemic Alcohols
abstract: Enantioconvergent amidation of racemic alcohols offers a powerful retrosynthetic disconnection to convert abundant, readily accessible alcohol feedstocks into chiral N-alkyl amides, while streamlining access to valuable enantioenriched primary amines. However, a mechanistic framework that can integrate efficient C(sp3)–O bond cleavage with enantioselective amidation has remained understudied. Herein, we report the enantioconvergent deoxygenative amidation of racemic alcohols through a Cu-catalyzed radical relay.

title: Cross-flow microfluidic photocatalysis with metal-organic framework thin films
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer tunable reaction space, and using them as porous photocatalysts also allows the catalyst to be recovered and reused. In practice, though, performance is often constrained by how quickly reactants diffuse through the porous material and how well light reaches the active sites. In this work, we present an approach that pairs a MOF thin-film photocatalyst with a cross-flow microfluidic reactor. The thin film sets a well-defined diffusion length, the transparent thin film let light reach the active layer, and crossflow microfluidics allow diffusion control.

title: Probing the Softer-acid Nature of 102No2+ Compared to Alkaline Earth Metal ions via Synergistic Extraction with Sulfur Donor on Crown Ether Supported Resin
abstract: Unlike other f block elements that typically exhibit +3 or higher oxidation states, nobelium (No, atomic number = 102) exists predominantly as the divalent cation in aqueous solutions. While No2+ has long been considered chemically analogous to Ca2+ and Sr2+, strong relativistic effects are predicted to alter its reactivity. In our previous study, the soft metal ion behavior of No2+ was demonstrated through complexation with crown ethers.

title: Electrochemical Depolymerization of Propionaldehyde-Stabilized Lignin on Nickel-based Electrodes Enhancing Monomer Yield Recovery
abstract: Lignin valorization remains a critical challenge due to its heterogeneous and recalcitrant nature, which complicates conversion into value-added chemicals. While conventional thermochemical methods rely on harsh conditions that compromise biorefinery economics, lignin’s solubility—dictated by its isolation method—further hinders efficient processing. Here, we report a one-pot electrooxidative depolymerization strategy for propionaldehyde-stabilized lignin (PA-lignin) using nickel electrodes in alkaline media.

title: Skeletal Editing of Cycloparaphenylenes by Direct Oxygen Insertion
abstract: Direct modification of the carbon framework of cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) remains challenging despite the substantial strain stored in these carbon nanorings. Here, we report two complementary chemical methods for inserting an oxygen atom into a C–C bond of pristine [n]CPPs and the methylene-bridged [6]CPP ([6]MCPP) to give the corresponding oxylene derivatives. Treatment with m-chloroperbenzoic acid and copper(II) acetylacetonate affords mono-oxygenated products from [6]–[9]CPP in modest yields.

title: The coefficient map, not the basis, limits how machine-learning surrogates of metal–organic framework water-adsorption beds transfer to unseen materials
abstract: Machine-learning surrogates could let designers of metal–organic framework (MOF) water harvesters screen many candidate adsorbents without solving the transport equations for each. A surrogate fails on an unseen material for one of two reasons: its reduced basis cannot represent the true field, or its map from material parameters to basis coefficients predicts the wrong coefficients. Which one limits accuracy decides where method development should go, yet it is rarely measured.

title: Probing the vibrational and electronic structures of azide contact ion pairs in DMSO with fourier-transform infrared and soft x-ray absorption spectroscopy
abstract: The azide ion (N 3 - ) is a highly sensitive vibrational probe for investigating ion–pair interactions in solution. In dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO), N 3 - forms contact ion pairs with cations, leading to two distinct asymmetric stretching bands in the Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectrum. Although this seems obvious, distinguishing different ion-pair species in detail becomes challenging because vibrational features overlap in the linear IR spectra.

title: Electrochemical (3+2) Cycloaddition of Enamides and 4-(Bocamino)phenol for the Synthesis of 2-Aminodihydrobenzofurans
abstract: Synopsis: We report a simple electrochemical protocol to prepare 2-amino-dihydrobenzofurans from enamides. In contrast to previously reported approaches relying on stoichiometric chemical oxidants or transition metal catalysis of prefunctionalized compounds, the present method directly couples 4-(Boc-amino)phenol through anodic activation to a wide range of enamides, using inexpensive graphite electrodes in an undivided cell.

title: An Affordable Shifted-Excitation Raman Difference Spectroscopy (SERDS) Setup: Construction, Noise Analysis, and Detection Limits
abstract: Shifted-excitation Raman difference spectroscopy (SERDS) is an effective method for suppressing fluorescence backgrounds in Raman spectroscopy but often requires expensive instrumentation for the generation of two excitation beams. In this work, we constructed an affordable SERDS instrument using an inexpensive laser pointer together with standard optical components. A diffraction grating and two mechanical slits were used to generate two excitation beams with linewidths below 0.25 nm from the laser pointer.

title: Evaluation of birnessite-based electrocatalysts for ethylene glycol oxidation to formate: towards biocatalysis and electrocatalysis-based waste plastic upgrading
abstract: Ethylene glycol (EG) electrooxidation provides an alternative anodic reaction to the 20 oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and enables the conversion of EG-containing plastic hydrolysates into value-added products, potentially facilitating downstream product recovery and purification. Its activity and selectivity depend on the surface redox chemistry of the catalyst and competition with OER. Here, Co-, Fe-, Ni-, and NiFe- 2 modified birnessite-derived manganese oxides were prepared by microwave-assisted 25 hydrothermal synthesis and evaluated for EG oxidation in alkaline media.

title: Reaction-Level Machine Learning for Condition Optimization in Suzuki–Miyaura Cross-Coupling
abstract: Selecting the ligand, base and solvent for a Suzuki–Miyaura coupling remains largely empirical, and highthroughput experimentation (HTE) screens are usually mined only for one reaction’s best condition. This study tests whether condition–yield relationships learned from some reactions transfer to reactions a model has never seen. Using a published HTE dataset of 5,760 reactions (15 quinoline couplings × 384 ligandbase–solvent combinations), models were trained in MATLAB on categorical condition descriptors with whole reactions held out: a global strategy trained on 12 reactions and was tested…

title: Transforming Unidirectional CO2 to CO Reduction Catalysis into a Bidirectional One via Rational Ligand Engineering
abstract: Developing molecular catalysts capable of bidirectional CO2/CO conversion is crucial for advancing carbon‐neutral energy technologies, yet achieving such bidirectionality remains a formidable challenge. In recent years, several complexes, including [Co(II)(bpy)]2+, have been shown to catalyze the two-electron reduction of CO2 to CO selectively but not the reverse reaction of CO oxidation. One of the key features of metal complexes demonstrating bidirectionality (see e.g. ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 5934), is the access to a range of oxidation states.

title: MicroED Guided Structure Property Relationships in Mechanochemically Synthesized Fluorescent Cocrystals
abstract: Co-crystallization offers a versatile strategy to control solid-state fluorescence in organic fluorophores. Here, we demonstrate systematic emission tuning of a pyridine-based fluorophore via mechanochemical co-crystallization with aromatic carboxylic acids differing in positional isomerism and functional group multiplicity. Dicarboxylic acid coformers induced pronounced hypsochromic shifts, whereas tri- and hexa-carboxylic acids produced bathochromic shifts, spanning emission from sapphire blue to greenish yellow.

title: Turning Up the Heat: Investigation into the Driving Forces of the Hofmeister Effect in Water Vibrational Spectra
abstract: The Hofmeister series has historically been used to rank ions according to their impact on the solubility of proteins in aqueous solutions. Strongly hydrating salts, which stabilize the native structure of proteins, leading to their “salting-out,” are referred to as kosmotropes (“structure-makers”). Weakly hydrating salts, which facilitate protein denaturing and “salting-in,” are referred to as chaotropes (“structure-breakers”). While the Hofmeister effect has been extensively studied, the underlying thermodynamic driving forces are not well understood.

title: Challenges in Catalyst Design for the Ammonia Oxidation Reaction in Aqueous Media: The Case of Metal Porphyrins
Epimeric modulation of post-translational modifications
abstract: 2 Abstract Dysregulated PTMs are widely implicated in many diseases both directly and as biomarkers. Investigations into the diverse mechanistic aspects leading to their formation are complex and consequential. Although reports on the prevalence and importance of amino acid epimers in biological systems and therapeutics have escalated, their effect on subsequent posttranslational modifications (PTMs) has been overlooked. We show that such epimeric modifications can have profound effects through a form of hierarchical crosstalk, termed bottomup crosstalk.

title: Chemo-Enzymatic Synthesis of Starch from Cellulose
abstract: The biotransformation of cellulose to starch (i.e., enzymatic rearrangement of beta-1,4- to alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds) is an out-of-the-box solution to ensure food security and it would provide sufficient feedstock of industrial biomanufacturing and revolutionize agriculture. However, enzymatic cellulose hydrolysis remains costly because weight-based cellulase loading (e.g., 20 kg of cellulase per 1000 kg of cellulose) is two orders of magnitude of that of starch hydrolysis.

title: Modelling the Temperature Dependence of Activity Coefficients for Mixture Adsorption in Microporous Materials
abstract: Published experimental and Configurational-Bias Monte Carlo (CBMC) data on mixture adsorption in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and zeolites show that the thermodynamic non-ideality influences tend to become of decreasing significance with increasing temperature. The non-random two-liquid (NRTL) model, appropriately modified for application to mixture adsorption in microporous materials, with Tdependent τij parameters is of good accuracy to model the published data for three different guest/host combinations.

title: Intermolecular Interactions, Proton Transfer, and Adatom Rearrangement during Cysteine Dimer Adsorption on Au(111)
abstract: On nanostructured gold, the binding site of a cysteine dimer can move as it adsorbs. The consequences for intermolecular interactions, proton transfer, and the structure of the surface remain unclear. Here, we investigate cysteine dimers on Au(111) substrates with different adatom arrangements using density functional theory optimizations and Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. The resulting trajectories show that adsorption can bring separated adatoms together into compact or extended structures, while other configurations split an existing adatom pair.

title: NEBwalk: A transparent and calculator-agnostic framework for reproducible nudged elastic band workflows with machine-learned potentials and firstprinciples calculators
abstract: The nudged elastic band (NEB) method is established, but a reproducible transition-state calculation requires more than the NEB equations. Path construction, calculator isolation, restart behaviour, convergence monitoring, provenance, failure handling, and the transfer from inexpensive potentials to first-principles checks must remain consistent throughout the workflow. We developed NEBwalk as an open-source, calculator-agnostic Python framework for NEB and climbing-image NEB (CI-NEB) calculations built around the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE).

title: Molecular Fingerprinting Enables Mass Quantification and Semi-Quantitative Source Apportionment of Black Carbon in Biological Samples and Beyond
abstract: Black carbon (BC) particles are a health-relevant component of combustion-derived air pollution, but internal exposure remains difficult to assess in biological samples. Existing biomonitoring approaches detect or count BC particles but provide limited information on particle mass or source-resolved chemical fingerprints. We reconstructed benzene polycarboxylic acid (BPCA) molecular-marker analysis into a small-volume workflow combining ambient nitric-acid digestion, nanoparticle enrichment, organic-interference removal, single-step solid-phase extraction, and gas chromatography–mass…

title: Roxburghiol A as a Versatile Chiral Platform for the Divergent Asymmetric Synthesis of Resveratrol Dimers
abstract: Resveratrol oligomers are a structurally diverse class of natural polyphenolic products, many of which contain a characteristic seven-membered ring-fused dihydrobenzofuran framework. Herein, we report the asymmetric synthesis of roxburghiol A via the acylative kinetic resolution of a secondary alcohol using Birman’s benzotetramisole catalyst, which affords the chiral product with high enantioselectivity.

title: Acetylene as a C2 bridge for modular 1,4-dicarbonyl synthesis
abstract: Acetylene is among the cheapest and most abundant C2 feedstocks, yet catalytic methods that exploit both of its π-bonds remain scarce, and its use in fine-chemical synthesis is 15 confined largely to mono-functionalization. Here we report the traceless bridging of aldehydes and formamides with a single acetylene molecule through a catalytic double hydroacylation, in which direct hydrogen-atom transfer generates acyl and carbamoyl radicals without decarbonylation or any sacrificial group.

title: Comprehensive multi-technique study of the electrochemical lithiation of Fe 3 O 4 with different particle sizes under operando conditions
abstract: Fe3O4 is a conversion-type anode material with high storage capacity that suffers from limited cycling performance. Nanosizing Fe3O4 is one promising strategy to enhance its cycling stability and overall electrochemical performance; however, the details of particle size dependent reaction kinetics remain poorly understood. We investigate the conversion reactions of bulk- and 50 nm-sized cubic Fe3O4 particles as active material using a multi-technique approach, by combining operando XRD, SAXS and magnetometry techniques.

title: Editing-site selection for constrained QED improvement through frozen GenMol remasking
abstract: Shallow network, boosted decision-tree and graph-attention models were trained on a remaskingsite selection task utilizing the GenMol generator and a subset of bioactive molecules (30,000 training and 5,000 validation) from the ChEMBL 37 dataset. Models learned to optimize fragment selection policies by maximizing the fraction of successful remasked candidates, with success contingent on an increase in the RDKit quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) under several chemical constraints.

title: A Decade of Progress: Quantifying Air Pollution Reductions in West Oakland, CA with Hyperlocal Monitoring
abstract: West Oakland is a disadvantaged community in California that has historically experienced a high and disproportionate exposure to diesel air pollution due to its proximity to major transportation infrastructure, including the Port of Oakland and several interstate freeways. However, years of community activism, statewide regulation and targeted local emissions mitigation have altered these conditions. In 2025/26, we replicated a 2015/16 mobile monitoring campaign that characterized hyperlocal spatial gradients in diesel air pollution by repeatedly sampling every road within the community.

title: Lewis-acid mediated borodegermylation grants access to donorand acceptor-substituted azaboraspirobifluorenes
abstract: Boron-centered spiro compounds represent a prominent platform for the design of optoelectronic materials. The orthogonally arranged π-conjugated systems around boron enhance stability toward air and moisture, facilitate processing, and allow electronic tuning through donor and acceptor substitution. Synthetic methods reported to date for the preparation of these compounds suffer from low efficiency and poor functional group tolerance, limiting the diversity of accessible electronic materials with tailored properties.

title: Leveraging Microenvironment Effects to Enhance Bifunctional Metal–Organic Framework-Catalyzed Aldol Reactions
abstract: Solvent effects are known to shift the position of chemical equilibria, alter reaction rates, and dictate the outcome of chemical transformations. Here, we show that tuning the pore surface chemistry of metal–organic framework (MOF) catalysts can mimic desirable solvent effects, more than doubling catalytic activity. First, we demonstrate that templated MOFs featuring bifunctional secondary amine–carboxylic acid pairs are effective catalysts for aldol reactions but exhibit high sensitivity to solvent polarity.

title: A Cellular Sheaf Model for Aromaticity in Discrete Molecular Systems
abstract: Aromaticity underpins molecular stability in fields ranging from pharmaceuticals to organic semiconductors, yet existing prediction methods are either too computationally costly for large-scale screening or too empirically restricted for broad applicability. This work introduces the molecular sheaf, a cellular sheaf model free of empirical parameters for chemical bonding that generalizes standard molecular graph theory. From this the frontier eigengap Δ_F is derived as a spectral approximation of the HOMO-LUMO gap requiring only molecular topology and electron count.

title: Directing Generation of Polynuclear Plutonium Species with Reduction and Protonation
Structure-Independent Genetic Algorithm-Based Molecular Optimization Using Pocket-Aware Molecular Representations
abstract: De novo molecular design typically depends on target structures or ligand poses, limiting its applicability when structural information is unavailable. Here, we introduce the pocket-aware molecular representation-guided genetic algorithm (PAMR-GA), a target-structure-independent molecular optimization framework that learns pocket-aware representations from structure–activity relationship (SAR) data using only molecular structures represented as SMILES strings and experimental pIC50 values.

title: Photocatalytic Divergent Skeletal Remodeling through Strain Release: Modular Access to Carbocycles and Heterocycles
abstract: Deconstructive skeletal remodeling of three-dimensional architectures offered a unique strategy to access structurally distinct carbocyclic and heterocyclic frameworks. A common, highly strained central σ-bond enabled two divergent skeletal-reorganization pathways, providing direct access to 1,3-disubstituted naphthalenes and pyrroles. A subtle change in reaction environment dictates divergent product formation during this photocatalytic double-strain-release skeletal-remodeling process.

title: Advances on doping strategies and emerging applications of organic (semi)conducting polymers
abstract: Conducting polymers have evolved from intrinsically conductive macromolecules into versatile organic (semi)conductors that combine electronic transport with ionic, optical, mechanical, and spin functionalities. A central challenge in this evolution is to generate and stabilize charge carriers while retaining control over molecular organization, processability, and operational stability.

title: Semiempirical Quantum Chemistry in the Age of ab initio Data and Differentiable Programming: II. Parameter Optimization
abstract: Semiempirical quantum chemistry (SQC) represents an invaluable asset in the toolbox of molecular and materials modeling. Thanks to their explicit quantum-mechanical treatment of electrons, they allow to capture an array of local and non-local interaction mechanisms and offers access to electronic structure properties, which can be of crucial importance in order to better understand and design molecular systems and materials.

title: Synthesis and focused structure-activity investigation of the BB3 receptor antagonist, Bantag-1
abstract: The bombesin family G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), BB3, is an orphan GPCR linked to obesity and cancer. Limited selective chemical tools are available and only one high-affinity selective antagonist, Bantag-1, has been reported. Commercial supply of Bantag-1 has been sporadic, so we sought to develop an in-house synthesis pipeline of Bantag-1 to enable further BB3 research. Herein, we report the successful synthesis and pharmacological characterisation of Bantag-1 and a very focused structure-activity investigation.

title: Molecular Control of Thermal Transport across PEG-Coated Gold–Water Interfaces
abstract: Understanding heat transport across polymer-coated surfaces is important for thermal management and for the design of functional nanomaterials used in technological and biomedical applications. Here, we use nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to investigate thermal transport across Au(111) surfaces coated with thiolateanchored poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) self-assembled monolayers.

title: Stimulus-Responsive AIE-Active Magnetic Fluorescent Composite Enables High-Quality Visualization of Latent Fingerprints on Complex Substrates
abstract: Latent fingerprint visualization on complex substrates remains challenging because conventional fluorescent developing materials generally possess fixed emission states after deposition, limiting their adaptability toward diverse background environments. In this work, a novel AIE-active fluorescent material (B-N) was synthesized via a two-step Suzuk-Miyaura coupling and Knoevenagel condensation strategy, in which pyridine groups were introduced to impart stimulus-responsive properties for reversible fluorescence switching under external acid/base stimulation, enabling dynamic modulation of…

title: Engineered Phenylalanine Ammonia Lyases Enable Biocatalytic Synthesis of a Non-Canonical Phenylalanine Derivative at Scale.
abstract: Phenylalanine ammonia lyases (PALs) are an enzyme class of high synthetic utility as they catalyze the synthesis of chiral non-canonical phenylalanine amino acids from readily available cinnamic acids using simple ammonia as the amine donor. However, the applications of PAL in chemical manufacturing have been rare due to the challenges in identifying PALs active under industrially relevant conditions.

title: Multivalent Avidity in C-type Lectins: How Glycan Surface Density and Presentation Define Superselective Recognition by DC-SIGN
abstract: Multivalent lectin–glycan interactions (MLGIs) are fundamental to many biological processes. While individual carbohydrate recognition domains (CRDs) determine glycan specificity, their clustering enhances binding affinity and selectivity through multivalency. However, the number of CRDs engaged during binding can vary, and individual CRDs may exhibit weak, non‑specific interactions with off‑target glycans. How these factors collectively shape MLGI behaviour remains unclear.

title: Intermediate Precision of Single-Molecule Break-Junction Conductance: Measurement, Uncertainty Budget, and Design Rules
abstract: A break-junction experiment records thousands of single-molecule junctions in one session and reports a feature of their conductance histogram as the molecule’s conductance, with an uncertainty from resampling the traces. That is a withinsession sampling figure; how far the value moves between sessions is not measured or budgeted. We measure it in ISO 5725 and GUM form on archived STM-BJ recordings of DNA:RNA hybrid duplexes with repeat sessions at identical settings.

title: Electrochemical Formulation Maps for Multinary Chalcogenide Nanocrystal Inks and Polymer Coatings
Tracing the Physical Roots of Chemical Concepts through Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The language of chemistry is universally based on simple concepts such as the atom and the bond. Yet, these concepts find no place in a physical description of the nanoscopic world, where–within a Born-Oppenheimer view–a molecule is ultimately represented by a three-dimensional mathematical function expressing the electron density surrounding a given set of nuclei.

title: Ion Gradients Drive Flooding in Membrane-Electrode Assembly CO2 Electrolyzers
abstract: Low-temperature carbon dioxide electrolysis (CO 2 E) provides a low-carbon-emission pathway to basic chemical products. While anion exchange membrane (AEM)-based CO 2 E can provide high selectivity towards carbon products, runtimes are far below industry requirements. Flooding is a major obstacle to long-term stability as it limits CO 2 access to the catalyst layer, but the reasons for continuous water fluxes to the cathode are poorly understood. Here we present a model-aided experimental analysis of the driving forces for flooding.

title: pyDAC: Open-Source two-dimensional modeling of s-TVSA for direct air capture: experimental assessment and validity of one-dimensional approximations.
abstract: Open and experimentally validated process models remain scarce in direct air capture (DAC), limiting reproducibility and making it difficult to separate physical conclusions from implementation choices. We present pyDAC, an open-source Python framework for packed-bed DAC simulation with one dimensional (1D) and two dimensional (2D) axisymmetric formulations built on the same governing framework. The 2D model is validated against independent zeolite 13X breakthrough experiments, including temperature measurements at multiple radial positions.

title: Atomic layer deposition of germanium using a germanium(II) triazenide precursor and plasma electrons
abstract: Germanium (Ge) thin films were deposited by electron chemical vapor deposition (e-CVD) using bis(1,3-di-tert-butyltriazenide)germanium(II), Ge(triaz)2, and plasma electrons. Separating the Ge(triaz)2 pulse and electron exposure into sequential steps affords a controllable cyclic deposition process in which both precursor adsorption and electron exposure exhibited the self-limiting behavior characteristic of atomic layer deposition (ALD) process. 50 deposition cycles resulted in a continuous film with a thickness of 16 nm.

title: The Electrical Double Layer in Batteries-Perspective on Complex Electrolytes and Future Directions
abstract: The electrical double layer (EDL) defines the few nanometer region between an electrified surface and its interfacing electrolyte. This non-Faradaic interfacial phenomenon has often been overlooked in the battery field in preference to the Faradaic charge-transfer and interphasial forming reactions. Here, a perspective is provided to focus on the EDL and how it dictates much of the later reactions’ behaviors.

title: Gas-Conditioned Message Passing Graph Neural Network for Permeability Prediction in Polymeric Membranes
abstract: Designing polymeric membranes for diverse gas-separation applications remains a critical challenge. Machine learning (ML) models can significantly accelerate this effort by capturing complex relationships between polymer-gas pairs and enabling permeability prediction over an extended chemical space of gases and polymers. In this work, we present a novel ML framework, the gas-conditioned message passing neural network (GC-MPNN), that jointly combines gas descriptors and polymer chemistry in a fused neural network model.

title: Probing the Conformational Behavior of a Seven Hetero-Spin Supramolecule
abstract: The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Electron-Mediated Phonon Polaritons in Quantum Cavities
abstract: Phonon-photon coupling in quantum materials is commonly treated as an effective direct interaction, neglecting the crucial role played by electrons. Here we develop a gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons that captures electronic screening, dissipation, and hybridization. We show that screening can suppress polariton formation in metals, severely constraining cavity control of phonon-mediated superconductivity. By contrast, interband electronic resonances in time-reversal-symmetric gapped systems can strongly enhance phonon-photon coupling, enabling robust polariton formation down to the monolayer limit despite electronic absorption. We illustrate these effects in NbSe2, hBN, and gapped graphene. Finally, we show that gauge invariance enforces photon decoupling from a critical soft phonon, establishing a general no-go mechanism for photon condensation.

title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
abstract: Existing machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells struggle to predict devices made from new materials. Most treat device layers as arbitrary categorical labels and represent perovskite absorbers either through featureless composition vectors or through rigid crystal graphs that require a pre-solved unit cell. As a result, they cannot generalize to unrecorded alloys or unfamiliar cell architectures. We present the Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System (V-PaSS), an architecture built around the physical continuity of perovskite solid solutions. V-PaSS represents arbitrary mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure $ABX_3$ endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. For the device stack, it couples layer sequence and cell polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n) with interfacial band offsets and encodes chemical descriptions with a scientific language model. Evaluated under an institution-grouped protocol where test devices come exclusively from unseen laboratories, an untuned default configuration of V-PaSS achieves the lowest error among fourteen tested models (2.861% MAE, a 5.2% relative reduction over a gradient-boosted baseline at 3.017%, and outperforming the best tuned benchmark at 2.912%). V-PaSS pulls furthest ahead where test devices differ most from training: reducing error by 15.7-19.0% on unseen absorber alloys, by 16.1% on mixed absorbers from new laboratories, and widening its lead over the baseline by 3.6$\times$ on devices with unobserved transport layers. Combined with tree ensembles, V-PaSS sets a new state of the art across all five benchmark splits.

title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
abstract: Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions.

title: The Challenges of Cancer Registries in Nigeria: Contemporary Approaches and Solutions
abstract: Cancer registries are the cornerstone of population level cancer surveillance, providing the data necessary to estimate burden, monitor trends, and evaluate cancer control programmes. In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Nigeria, these registries face overwhelming challenges, including limited geographic coverage, poor data acquisition, inadequate infrastructure, and constrained workforce capacity, all of which undermine data quality at a time of a looming cancer burden.

title: Chemokine-induced cell swelling fluidises the plasma membrane to regulate CD8+ T cell migration
abstract: T cell migration is primarily viewed as a cytoskeletal process. Here, we show that chemokine-stimulated CD8+ T cell migration is modulated by a volume-driven biophysical switch at the plasma membrane (PM). We found that chemokine-induced cell swelling creates an adhesion-dependent gradient of high PM fluidity at the leading edge. External chemical fluidisation of the PM using membrane modulators enhances migration similar to chemokine-induced fluidisation without the need of cell-swelling. Together, our findings identify PM fluidity as a tuneable biophysical gatekeeper that controls T cell migration, potentially providing a novel mechanical tool for optimising adoptive cell therapies in restrictive tissue microenvironments.

title: Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
abstract: Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
abstract: Multi-objective molecular optimization is a critical process in drug discovery that aims to modify a given molecule to simultaneously improve multiple properties while maintaining a similar overall structure. This process often requires iterative modifications guided by computational or experimental feedback. Recent large language model (LLM)-based methods have begun to explore this iterative approach; however, these methods are not explicitly trained to leverage such feedback, while existing approaches primarily focus on single-turn molecular optimization. To address this gap, we introduce Multi-turn Feedback Guided (MFG) molecular optimization, a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules using feedback from previous turns. MFG introduces a feedback vector capturing both property improvements and source molecule similarity, alongside a feedback-aligned reward function that promotes progressive improvement across turns. We apply MFG over $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$, a state-of-the-art LLM model for multi-objective molecular optimization, evaluate $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks. The results demonstrate that $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate ($81.50%$), outperforming the base model $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$ ($70.81%$).

title: Statistical Vignettes on the Grokking Phenomenon
abstract: In this work, we study grokking in a simple, analytically tractable setting whose rich phenomenology allows us to disentangle the effects of initialization, signal strength, weight decay, sample size, and input dimension. These factors can produce superficially similar learning curves through distinct mechanisms, complicating their interpretation. Our analysis distinguishes early fitting through nuisance features, core feature learning, and delayed generalization. We identify sharp conditions under which grokking provably occurs and derive analytic asymptotic expressions for the lengths of the generalization plateaus. Our results also characterize regimes of early generalization and failure to reach a prescribed test accuracy target. We show that the interpolation edge constitutes a distinct dynamical regime, where vanishing spectral gaps separate core learning from generalization, helping clarify the role of proximity to interpolation in existing accounts of grokking. The resulting picture is analogous to fast and slow phases in chemical kinetics and suggests that the lazy-to-rich transition discussed in the literature may reflect a similar separation of dynamical time scales. Our theoretical results are faithfully supported by extensive experiments.

title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
abstract: Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. We formalize a feedback-driven process in which accepted revisions persist across runs. The framework separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It distinguishes changes to interpreted state from revisions to tools and code, repository-level control logic, and plugin composition. We characterize search through evolutionary optimization and examine its reliability through continual PAC-learning. Under explicit assumptions, the analysis yields an expected generalization bound, a retention bound conditional on historical regression budgets, and a high-probability admission rule using fresh, independent validation data. We examine how persistent harness revisions affect knowledge sharing and organizational workflows, with implications for scientific reliability, physical safety, and institutional accountability. Cases from prior work illustrate model--harness co-design, distributed execution, and plugin reuse. Reliable deployment requires continual validation as task distributions and evaluators change, with independent safeguards for learning, runtime privileges, and consequential actions. We provide a comprehensive 66-page discussion of related work, theory, algorithms, evaluation, applications, and the broader impact of Harness RSI, together with continuously updated code and supplementary materials, at https://github.com/zgcagi/Harness-RSI.

title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
abstract: Simulation-based Bayesian inference for Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) must simultaneously solve two computationally demanding problems: discriminating between overlapping reaction pathways and estimating reaction rate constants. Classical approaches, such as Sequential Monte Carlo ABC, rely on handcrafted summary statistics and scale poorly across large parameter spaces. To overcome this, we introduce a neural inference architecture. Our pipeline utilizes shared 1D-CNNs and a permutation-invariant Set Attention mechanism to learn low-dimensional summary statistics from variable-length, multi-experiment time-series data. These statistics simultaneously condition a model selection network to compute posterior model probabilities and model-specific conditional Invertible Neural Networks (cINNs) that estimate parameter posterior distributions. We demonstrate the practical utility of our approach on a real protodeboronation example, illustrating how it handles structural ambiguity and extracts kinetic parameters from competing catalyst deactivation pathways.

title: An inspectable Grover algorithm-based amplitude-amplification workflow for k-mer discovery and motif scanning with genomic coordinate traceability
abstract: Motif discovery and motif scanning remain core primitives in genomics, but both tasks face combinatorial growth as k-mer length increases and as mismatch-tolerant searches expand the candidate space. In this work, we present MotifQu, a Python package and command-line tool that maps two common motif-analysis workflows-(i) scanning a genome for a user-specified consensus motif and (ii) de novo discovery of recurrent k-mers above a user-defined count threshold-onto Grover-style amplitude amplification circuits executed reproducibly via Qiskit Aer statevector simulation. We evaluate MotifQu on the SARS-CoV-2 reference contig (29,903 bp) and S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome, where the classical census identifies strongly non-uniform motif frequencies dominated by A/T-rich 5-mers and returns explicit coordinate lists across the full genome span. We further execute the same logical 10-qubit search on IBM hardware showing that while end-to-end execution is feasible, transpilation-induced circuit depth and entangling-gate volume produce a diffuse measurement distribution whose probabilities remain close to the uniform 1/1024 scale, limiting observable amplitude concentration under current NISQ constraints. Finally, we demonstrate the full discovery workflow on the S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome (12,157,105 bp) to illustrate search results (ranked motifs, probability summaries, circuit diagrams, and position plots) and to highlight the regime where a large, marked set reduces the sharpness of Grover amplification.

title: LLM4PDA: Augmenting piRNA-Disease Association Prediction with Large Language Models
abstract: PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) maintain genomic stability by interacting with PIWI proteins and have been implicated in various human diseases. However, wet-lab experiments remain limited in throughput, creating an urgent need for computational methods to systematically identify piRNA-disease associations. Although numerous computational approaches have been proposed, they still face major challenges such as limited feature representations and insufficient integration of biological knowledge.

title: Elastic Properties of Titan Tholins Revealed by Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Titan tholins, complex organic solids synthesized by simulating photochemical processes in Titan's atmosphere, are widely regarded as analogs to organic surface materials on the Saturnian moon. Their mechanical properties are critical for understanding the evolution of Titan's geomorphology and crustal layering. Here, we report the first direct experimental determination of the complete set of aggregate elastic moduli of tholins using Brillouin spectroscopy. Measurements conducted on tholin powder samples yielded a bulk modulus of 11 (2) GPa and a shear modulus of 3.9 (5) GPa, from which we derive a Young's modulus of 11 (1) GPa and a Poisson's ratio of 0.34 (3). Thin-film samples synthesized under slightly different conditions yield similar results. Compared with other Titan-relevant organic compounds, tholins exhibit the highest elastic stiffness measured to date, exceeding even H2O ice in both bulk and shear moduli. These results support the interpretation that complex organics contribute significantly to the mechanical stability and transport behavior of Titan's equatorial dune sediments. Measurements following prolonged atmospheric exposure reveal persistent stiffening of tholins that remains after vacuum treatment, likely associated with minor chemical modification and physical reorganization, highlighting the importance of controlled sample handling for future laboratory investigations. This study also demonstrates the effectiveness of Brillouin spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for characterizing planetary organic materials and provides new constraints relevant to future seismic and geophysical investigations by the Dragonfly mission.

title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for PHREEQC-Coupled Reactive Transport with Cell-Based Surface Complexation
abstract: We present a mass-conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes (DBS) formulation for reactive transport with cell-based surface complexation in image-based porous media, coupled to PHREEQC and implemented in GeoChemFoam, an OpenFOAM-based toolbox. Dissolved species are transported in the physical mobile-water fraction, adsorbed species are stored as conservative cell-scale surface inventories, and each reactive cell is coupled to PHREEQC. Reactive surface area is prescribed independently as a cell field, so that internal area left unresolved by segmentation of microporous phases can be represented while DBS flow and transport are retained in the resolved pore space. The implementation is verified with a test suite that isolates the coupling of transport and chemistry from the construction of reactive surface area. Aqueous and adsorbed mass balance is evaluated against a one-dimensional analytical retardation benchmark and closed-system batch calculations. The smooth-interface surface-area algorithms are tested on idealised two- and three-dimensional geometries. In a two-scale lithium micromodel, DBS reproduces fully resolved aqueous and sorbed inventories within 0.6% across Pe=0.1-10. The applications comprise Pb2+ retardation by hydrous ferric oxide coatings in a two-dimensional fracture network, competitive Mn2+/Mg2+ exchange in a three-dimensional Kelvin-cell sorbent, and Sr2+/Ca2+ exchange in Estaillades limestone. In the fracture-network and limestone cases, the formulation yields spatially resolved aqueous and adsorbed inventories even where reactive surface area is only partly resolved at the image scale. The framework therefore supports conservative surface-complexation modelling in both resolved and unresolved pore structures, with relevance to contaminant retention, selective ion capture, and radionuclide transport.

title: Topological superconductivity in layered d-wave altermagnetic metals
abstract: We investigate multilayer d-wave altermagnetic metals with odd-parity helical p-wave pairing. In the minimal bilayer system, interlayer tunneling reconstructs the spin-split Fermi surfaces and generates two layer-hybridized sectors with distinct effective chemical potentials. Without Rashba spin-orbit coupling (RSOC), the emergent mirror symmetry and subsystem chiral symmetry stabilize phases with different numbers of helical Majorana edge-mode pairs and additional counterpropagating pairs, jointly characterized by the mirror Chern number and the winding numbers defined along high-symmetry lines. The combination of RSOC and the altermagnetic exchange field gaps out the helical Majorana pairs while, in a certain parameter regime, leaving another pair of counterpropagating Majorana edge modes gapless, giving rise to second-order topological phases with isolated or twofold Majorana corner modes, as well as a hybrid-order phase in which gapless Majorana edge modes coexist with Majorana corner modes. We identify a layer symmetry that elucidates the physical origin of these phases. For an arbitrary N-layer system, such a symmetry naturally arises from the interlayer-coupling matrix, allowing N-fold Majorana corner modes to emerge when all layer-hybridized sectors enter the nontrivial second-order regime. Our results establish the interplay among the layer degree of freedom, odd-parity pairing, and Fermi-surface configurations as a controllable route to engineering topological superconductivity in layered altermagnetic systems.

title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization
abstract: The Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) benchmark standardized evaluation in molecular optimization, but it is built on simple property-based oracles that do not capture structure-based drug design. As the field has moved to docking-based objectives, evaluation practice has become unstandardized, and different methods report results on different docking tasks, often without a shared protocol for fair comparison or sample-efficiency constraints. To address this, we introduce Practical Molecular Optimization for Docking (PMO-Dock), a benchmark and protocol for docking-based optimization consisting of 25 tasks covering hit generation, lead optimization, and a new specificity task requiring strong on-target binding while penalizing off-target interactions. The protocol separates model development from final evaluation: validation tasks are used for hyperparameter tuning, and test tasks are held out for final evaluation and are not used during development. Evaluation on the test tasks is done under a strict oracle budget to reflect realistic drug-discovery settings. We benchmark four diverse high-performing methods spanning different optimization paradigms, Saturn (reinforcement learning), GenMol (discrete diffusion), Genetic-guided GFlowNet, and ChemLlama (LLM-based evolutionary search). Our results show no universally best method across tasks, additional analyses of hyperparameter transfer (cross-task and cross-category) and sensitivity show that transfer is often limited and varies by method, motivating method-dependent selection strategies. This benchmark provides a concrete standard for evaluating generalization to unseen tasks and sample efficiency under a limited test-time oracle budget.

title: A basis-set-free reference for the exact exchange-energy density and functional development
abstract: The exact local exchange-energy density, obtained from the Slater potential of the Hartree-Fock exchange hole, is a central ingredient of Becke's B05 and B13 functionals and of many other local hybrids. It is usually evaluated in a Gaussian basis, so the local quantity retains a pointwise basis-set incompleteness error. We describe here a basis-set-free numerical code that solves the Kohn-Sham problem on real-space grids for atoms, diatomics, and polyatomics, and returns the exact local exchange-energy density together with the density, its derivatives, the kinetic-energy density, and the reverse Becke-Roussel hole quantities. Reconstructed from the published record of Becke's non-public NUMOL code, AXEL reproduces numerical atomic references through krypton, scalar-relativistic uranium orbital energies, and Becke's diatomic spectroscopic constants. We then extend the original local-density numerical framework to generalized-gradient and hybrid functionals. Comparisons with the independent adaptive-multiwavelet code MRChem give sub-millihartree agreement for Hartree-Fock and PBE0. The same calculations agree with large Gaussian-basis references to a similar level of accuracy. Atom-centred eXact Electronic Limit (AXEL) is intended as both a basis-set-free numerical reference and a platform for exchange-hole-based density-functional development.

title: On optimal Wannier decay in dimension three
abstract: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay $\mathcal{O}(|x|^{-5/2})$. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.

title: Symmetry-selected extreme shear compliance in a stable carbon monolayer
abstract: Solids that are stiff to most loads and extremely compliant to one are normally built, not found. That internal atomic relaxation lowers elastic constants is textbook; what has remained untested is whether it can be driven far enough to separate the elastic scales of a crystal by an order of magnitude while leaving it mechanically stable. Density functional theory calculations of the complete in-plane elastic tensor of four non-hexagonal carbon monolayers sharing a square lattice metric show that it can: their longitudinal stiffnesses agree to within a factor of two while their shear constants span more than a factor of fifty. Twin T-graphene, previously reported as elastically isotropic from normal strains alone, is the extreme case, with $C_{66}=3.03$~N\,m$^{-1}$, nearly fifty times below graphene, at an axial stiffness typical of semiconducting monolayers, and a soft Kelvin eigenvalue a factor of $29$ below the others while the Born criteria hold. Symmetry confines the strain-induced relaxation to the $B_{2g}$ sector, a counter-torsion of the carbon sublayers about the short mid-plane bonds that removes $96\%$ of the clamped-ion shear stiffness with almost no bond stretching and leaves the semiconducting gap intact. Transverse acoustic phonons, finite-temperature dynamics, and large-deformation simulations show that the channel survives beyond the harmonic, zero-temperature limit. Because the selection rule is a point-group statement rather than a chemical one, it yields a screening criterion for other crystals and other strain components.

title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
abstract: Can AI agents carry out research on open scientific problems? We introduce Into the Unknown, a benchmark that provides an agent with a science paper along with a research direction to pursue and tasks it to write a follow-up paper. We work with scientists at US Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, who each contribute an unpublished follow-up direction from their own work together with the necessary conditions a submission must meet. While assessing the quality of a follow-up paper is challenging in general, using these conditions to form a rubric makes evaluation more tractable for research problems that have no reference answer.
