We have nine frontier agents write 15 follow-ups each, spanning quantum computing, plasma physics, computational chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning domains. None of the 135 submissions satisfies all the conditions, and 114 fail our integrity check, most often because the paper claims work that was never done or reports numbers that contradict the recorded evidence. Overall, agents readily produce papers that look like follow-ups, but none meets the standard of the domain scientist, leaving substantial headroom. Our code and data are publicly available.

title: PairIT: Autoregressive Transformers for Low-Data Molecule Optimization
abstract: Generating novel molecules with desired properties is a central challenge in drug discovery. Although foundational work focused on de novo generation, practical use cases require a more complex setting: conditioning on an initial seed molecule, optimizing multiple properties, and operating in data-sparse regimes. We introduce PairIT, a flexible training framework for autoregressive transformers over SMILES sequences that enables seeded generation by learning from pairs of structurally similar molecules. By leveraging matched pairs, the model learns to generate local, chemically meaningful edits that improve a property of the seed molecule. Prompt tokens extend this framework by specifying the target property, desired direction, and approximate magnitude of change. Multiple prompt tokens can be concatenated to enable multi-property optimization at inference time. For properties where pair supervision alone is insufficient, reinforcement learning post-training can further improve optimization, providing a tunable trade-off between proximity to the seed and the optimization objective. PairIT naturally supports pretraining on a large dataset and fine-tuning on a smaller dataset, which is critical for performance in data-sparse regimes. Surprisingly, we observe diminishing returns to the scale of the pretraining dataset. We demonstrate empirically on MoleculeNet and Therapeutics Data Commons datasets that, with appropriate paired-data curation, a standard transformer model of modest size (68M parameters) can achieve robust seeded molecular optimization in low-data regimes.

title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
abstract: Transparent conductors are key functional materials in modern optoelectronic devices. Their performance is governed by an inherent trade-off between optical transparency and electrical conductivity. Correlated metallic oxides offer an attractive workaround to this compromise, where narrow partially-filled bands provide high conductivity, while the absence of visible-range transitions enables optical transparency. Despite this promise, transparency and conductivity remain coupled through carrier density and electronic coherence. Here, we use proximity to a metal-insulator transition (MIT) as a design principle for engineering this balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors. Epitaxial Ti-substituted $SrVO_3$ films serve as a model platform where the optical window and metallicity are tuned simultaneously. We demonstrate and explain a systematic broadening of the optical window to regimes relevant for silicon photovoltaics. This gain is counterbalanced by carrier depletion and disorder, which drive the loss of coherent transport near the composition-driven MIT. A Haacke figure-of-merit analysis identifies the optimal composition range near the MIT, where the loss of metallic transport is accompanied by persistent near-Fermi-level spectral weight, indicating disorder-assisted localization together with correlation-driven spectral-weight redistribution. These findings establish proximity to an MIT as a general materials-design strategy, using electronic filling as a tuning knob for the transparency-conductivity balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors.

title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections to Quantum Ansätze
abstract: Circuit depth and measurement count are the main limitations for chemical applications of the leading variational quantum algorithms on quantum computers. We show that both resource requirements can be reduced by augmenting adaptive variational quantum algorithms with post-optimization corrective techniques. We focus on two such techniques---Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization and the identity-augmented quantum self-consistent equation of motion (q-sc-EOM)---applied to optimized ADAPT-VQE states without further ansatz growth or nonlinear optimization. Across molecular systems studied with up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduces the optimized iterations (and the corresponding number of adaptive layers) needed to reach the $1.6~\mathrm{m}E_h$ threshold by up to approximately sixfold, with a general trend toward larger reductions at higher determinant Rényi entropy. We also find measurement-cost reductions of up to approximately fortyfold using a suitable resource-cost model. Identity-augmented q-sc-EOM improves molecular potential-energy curves obtained from truncated ADAPT-VQE ansätze with limited expressivity and recovers accuracy from states produced by sampled operator ranking without additional gradient-based operator selection, providing an advantage when small pool gradients make selection measurement intensive. Together, these post-optimization corrections offer routes to improve energy accuracy and reduce adaptive circuit growth in quantum algorithms as quantum hardware advances.

title: Magnetic and Electrochemical Properties of the Altermagnetic Layered Antiperovskite Na2Mn2OS2
abstract: Incorporating multiple anions into perovskite-type frameworks provides a handle to design innovative lattices and trigger exotic properties. Inverse Lieb lattices have been receiving substantial interest as hosts for d-wave altermagnetism. One mixed-anion system in which these lattices have been experimentally realized is layered oxychalcogenides. By employing a high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis method, we introduce Na2Mn2OS2 as an additional member of this family of compounds. Na2Mn2OS2 adopts an antiperovskite-derived structure, consisting of layers of face-sharing MnO2S4 octahedra.

title: Deep chemometrics for retrospective auditing of the water-nutrient nexus in olive oil via 1D-CNN and explainable AI
abstract: Transitioning toward high-value functional food markets increases demand for forensic tools capable of verifying the "water-nutrient nexus", the complex agronomic interplay between irrigation and fertilization that shapes olive oil composition and authenticity. Conventional chemometrics often fail to capture synergistic, non-linear cultivation fingerprints within complex chemical matrices. This study introduces a "Deep Chemometrics" framework for retrospective auditing of olive oil history using FTIR spectroscopy and a customized one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN).

title: Mapping Synthetic Circuit Design Space through Massively Parallel Measurement of Single-Cell Dynamics
abstract: Engineering predictable and robust gene-regulatory networks requires a quantitative understanding of how their dynamics depend on genetic design and environmental conditions. To investigate these relationships, we introduce BARRACUDA, a high-throughput platform that combines combinatorial assembly and programmable perturbations with lineage-resolved time-lapse imaging and optical pooled screening. Experiments using this platform follow approximately one million cell lineages, collectively sampling tens of thousands of circuit designs. We used BARRACUDA to investigate how the robustness of circuit behavior depends on molecular components and their interactions, combining quantitative dynamic measurements with precise genetic and environmental control. Antithetic integral feedback provided a model system linking a defined molecular architecture to theoretical predictions of robust adaptation. Through a hierarchy of increasingly complex libraries, we characterized individual components and used those measurements to model and interpret the dynamics of complete feedback circuits. Circuits built from wild-type inhibitory proteins rejected disturbances but also exhibited sustained overadaptation and fast disturbance-induced oscillations unexplained by a reduced control model. These discrepancies motivated a screen of de novo binders that retained inhibitory function while reducing host-stress response. Selected de novo binders supported strong feedback regulation and robust performance in the rebuilt circuits. Across more than 20,000 recovered feedback-circuit variants, binder identity and controller expression organized regimes of strong regulation and sustained oscillation. Counterintuitively, disturbances sometimes improved compensation rather than compromising it, consistent with nonlinear changes in feedback engagement. Together, these results show how structured libraries and massively parallel measurements of single-cell dynamics can test mechanistic theories across scales of circuit complexity, reveal missing biological interactions, and map the design space of gene-regulatory networks.

title: Quantifying RNA Folding Equilibria from Unclassified Cryo-EM Particle Images
abstract: Functional RNA structures are typically far more dynamic than most proteins solved by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). Flexible junctions and weak tertiary contacts produce broad conformational ensembles, and cryo-EM particle classification analyses discard unaligned particles, which inherently contain the information needed to quantify such broad ensembles. Here, we infer compositional and conformational distributions from unclassified particle images by Bayesian ensemble reweighting. We tested our approach on the P4-P6 domain of the Tetrahymena thermophila group I intron, a classic model system of Mg2+-dependent RNA folding. While stable monomeric and dimeric states yielded high-resolution reconstructions, analyses of abundant, flexible conformations required Bayesian ensemble inference. Our approach quantitatively captured the Mg2+-dependent folding transition, indicating that cryo-EM can report the abundance of coexisting RNA states in agreement with bulk solution measurements. These results showcase how quantitative studies of RNA folding can be achieved by combining cryo-EM measurements with statistical ensemble-inference tools.

title: Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
abstract: Energetic materials involve multiple interactions, making reliable machine-learning potentials (MLPs) difficult to construct without extensive datasets. Here, we enhance the ability of the neural network interatomic potential (NNAP) to describe molecular systems using sphmulti, a refined spherical-harmonic basis set that combines extra radial basis with element-specific chemical weighting in each radial channel. We further integrate hyperactive learning, farthest-point sampling, and iterative sufficiency criteria with knowledge-guided key events, enabling the NNAP to retain essential information for describing the material system. For 3,3'-diamino-4,4'-azoxyfurazan, the resulting NNAP is trained on only 13,680 configurations yet captures key properties, including the isomerization barrier, pyrolysis activation energy, and shock Hugoniot behavior. NNAP-driven molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that pyrolysis proceeds through furazan-ring opening followed by chain reactions, whereas shock loading induces anisotropic hydrogen transfer driven by interlayer structural deformations. This work enables efficient and reliable MLPs for energetic materials.

title: Direct view of exciton and carrier dynamics in twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) on H-intercalated SiC (twist angle of $9 \pm 1^{\circ}$) is studied by position\mbox{-}, time\mbox{-}, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). Both graphene layers are hole doped, with a Dirac-point offset of 30~meV. Time-resolved ARPES near the van Hove singularity reveals a spectral feature within the hybridization-induced band gap, together with excited electrons in the conduction band. The in-gap feature exhibits distinct dynamics, and its binding energy and $k$-space location are consistent with the proposed non-hydrogenic ``ghost-Fano'' exciton arising from destructive interference between two nearly degenerate excitonic channels. Near the Dirac points, the twist separates the largely layer-polarized Dirac cones in momentum space, providing direct layer selectivity. We find markedly different peak electronic temperatures in the two graphene layers, even though their subsequent cooling dynamics are very similar. We attribute this to an ultrafast interlayer redistribution of electronic energy, driven by an interlayer electric field that arises from the different doping in the layers.

title: WannierSTM: Efficient superconducting scanning-probe spectroscopy from maximally localized Wannier functions
abstract: We present a Python-based program that combines maximally localized Wannier functions-based first-principles electronic structure with the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism to enable efficient simulations of scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The workflow builds upon standard density functional theory packages to construct compact transport Hamiltonians that preserve the properties of realistic materials. Superconductivity is incorporated via an effective pairing potential within the Nambu-spinor formalism, while coupling to the STM tip and substrate electrodes is treated using the wide-band limit approximation. Within this formulation, transport quantities such as current-voltage characteristics and differential conductance are evaluated in a closed analytical form. This avoids explicit numerical energy integrations and enables rapid spectroscopic calculations over broad parameter spaces. The framework provides a unified and computationally efficient approach for modeling superconducting hybrid nanostructures with spin-orbit coupling, magnetic textures, and spin polarization. Representative applications in spin chains, two-dimensional and molecular magnets on a superconductor demonstrate its robust capabilities for both simple model systems and realistic ab initio molecular structures relevant to modern STM experiments.

title: Field-free Magnetoacoustic Nonreciprocity via Exchange-bias Engineering
abstract: Nonreciprocal wave propagation is essential for directional signal processing and isolation. Magnetoacoustic systems are attractive platforms for nonreciprocal devices because of their small footprint and passive operation. However, pronounced nonreciprocity typically requires an external bias field,limiting device miniaturization and integration. Here, we demonstrate field-free magnetoacoustic nonreciprocity in an IrMn/FeGaB/Cu/FeGaB multilayer integrated with a shear-horizontal-wave delay line. Exchange-bias engineering stabilizes a remanent magnetic state with broken time-reversal and spatial-inversion symmetries while tailoring the spin-wave dispersion to achieve resonant magnetoacoustic coupling at zero field. The normalized isolation reaches 21 dB/mm, with its sign programmable by the field-sweep history. Further numerical optimization predicts a zero-field normalized isolation of 91 dB/mm by increasing the dynamical magnetic asymmetry. Our work establishes exchange-bias engineering as a promising route toward compact RF isolators and circulators and as a general strategy for realizing magnetoacoustic devices without external magnetic fields.

title: All-electron machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems
abstract: We introduce STRUCTURES-P, a machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems. Electrostatics are evaluated analytically in an atom-centered Gaussian basis, while an equivariant network learns the kinetic and exchange-correlation energy from energies and gradients of non-ground-state densities. Minimizing the functional from a superposition of atomic densities recovers the Kohn-Sham ground state: on held-out crystals, the density error falls from 6.7% to 0.4% of the electron count and the energy error reaches 0.25 mHa per atom, half that of a same-architecture interatomic potential. A single functional can be trained for both isolated molecules and periodic systems, and the model generalizes to larger unit cells. It largely preserves relative-energy rankings and reproduces convex-hull vertices on the tested H-N composition slice. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of machine-learned all-electron orbital-free DFT for variational density optimization and energy evaluation in fixed-geometry solids.

title: LinMorph: Learning to Morph Weights for Efficient Video DiT Linearization
abstract: Post-hoc linearization is an attractive way to accelerate pretrained Video Diffusion Transformers (Video DiTs), yet existing methods largely treat the quality loss induced by attention replacement as a recovery problem. We show that a more fundamental bottleneck lies upstream: \emph{initialization}. Random initialization discards pretrained knowledge, whereas manual weight reuse transfers it through rigid and incomplete source--target correspondences. We introduce \textbf{LinMorph}, which recasts Video DiT linearization as a learnable softmax-to-linear weight transformation problem. Instead of copying predefined counterparts, LinMorph learns a cross-parameter morphism that lets each target Gated DeltaNet (GDN) parameter draw jointly from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including for parameters with no direct softmax counterpart. A single morphism is shared across layers and learned through local teacher alignment, while producing layer-specific initializations from their respective pretrained weights. The resulting weights are then materialized as independent GDN modules for progressive distillation and joint recovery.Since the morphism operates in weight space rather than token space, it can be learned on short, low-resolution clips and directly reused at larger video scales. Across pretrained Video DiTs, LinMorph enables markedly faster recovery and better final generation quality than random initialization and heuristic weight reuse. Results show that efficient linearization depends not only on how a converted model is recovered, but critically on how pretrained knowledge is transferred before recovery. Project page: https://lonelyling.github.io/LinMorph.

title: Prospective discovery of LasB inhibitors by integrating generative design, free energy ranking, and experimental validation
abstract: Identifying synthetically accessible, potent ligands from vast chemical space remains a major challenge in drug discovery, particularly because experimental synthesis and testing are costly and low throughput. Here, we present a fully open-source computational-experimental workflow that integrates fragment-based de novo molecular design with rigorous alchemical absolute binding free-energy calculations to enable physics-based prioritization before chemical synthesis. We apply this strategy by targeting the virulence-associated zinc metalloprotease LasB from Pseudomonas aeruginosa. From ~40,000 diverse compounds generated through multi-objective optimization, a small subset was prioritized and experimentally evaluated, leading to the discovery of three previously unreported nanomolar inhibitors (IC50 22-53 nM) with excellent metabolic and plasma stability. This work demonstrates a general and scalable framework for coupling generative molecular design with quantitative binding affinity prediction, improving decision-making and reducing the cost, time, and risk associated with early-stage drug discovery.

title: Interlaboratory benchmarking of differential scanning fluorimetry reveals sources of variability in protein thermal stability parameters
abstract: Differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF) is widely used to assess protein thermal stability and to compare protein variants, ligands, or formulations with limited sample consumption. Yet, the reproducibility of DSF derived parameters across laboratories, instruments and analysis workflows remains poorly defined. Here, we report a two phase interlaboratory benchmark using a shared VHH sample across 26 laboratories, 28 instruments and seven DSF instrument models. In Phase 1, participants applied their routine acquisition and analysis workflows, whereas in Phase 2, acquisition conditions were harmonised. Datasets were analysed locally and then centrally reprocessed with MoltenProt. Participant reported apparent melting temperatures (Tm) showed good within instrument repeatability but moderate inter instrument dispersion. Harmonisation of acquisition conditions did not substantially reduce this dispersion. Conversely, centralised reprocessing narrowed the distribution among retained datasets, indicating contributions from analysis workflows and data acceptance criteria in addition to instrument dependent factors. Comparison with differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further showed that apparent Tm depended strongly on the fluorescence readout. For this VHH, single wavelength fluorescence at 350 nm showed the closest agreement with the DSC transition temperature, whereas the 350/330 nm ratio and barycentric mean generally yielded higher values. Furthermore, DSF derived apparent unfolding enthalpies were more variable than apparent Tm. Together, these findings show that DSF can be highly repeatable within a defined instrument and workflow, but that quantitative comparability across instruments depends on instrument specific effects, the choice of fluorescence readout and analysis strategy. Improved comparability will require transparent reporting of acquisition and analysis conditions, explicit data quality criteria, and well characterised reference materials to monitor instrument dependent offsets.

title: Metasurface information processor based on 4D bionic hardware and software for ultralow energy consumption computing
abstract: As AI technology faces an energy crisis, one promising solution is bionic ultra-low energy computing hardware, which can operate at a power level as low as sub-20-watt based on the 4D model of Ca 2+ channels recently verified in brain information processing. Inspired by this model, here we design and fabricate a 4D bionic computing system based on information metasurface array with the powerful capability of electromagnetic controls.

title: On the Mathematical Structure of Helical Shear in Anelastic Continua
abstract: We study helical shear of a thick-walled tube made of an incompressible, isotropic hyper-anelastic solid carrying a radially symmetric distribution of axial screw dislocations. Through the Bilby--Kröner--Lee decomposition, the dislocations are encoded in a Weitzenböck material manifold, whose Riemannian metric alone enters the elastic response. Equilibrium reduces at each radius to an algebraic system for the azimuthal and axial shear strains, whose cross terms are proportional to the dislocation strength and to the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant; the two shear modes therefore couple only in the presence of dislocations. Exact solutions are obtained for neo-Hookean, Fung--Demiray, Gent, Knowles, and Mooney--Rivlin materials, and numerical ones for Gent--Gent materials. The universal relations of Horgan and Saccomandi are extended to dislocated generalized neo-Hookean tubes. Dislocations stiffen the tube when the strain energy stiffens with the first invariant, couple the two shear modes chirally when it depends on the second, and may restrict admissibility: they cap the dislocation strength in Gent and Gent--Gent materials, and contract the admissible traction region in Knowles materials with power-law index below n = 1/2. A weakly nonlinear analysis to third order in the applied tractions and dislocation strength shows that, at first order (linear elasticity), the dislocations leave the shear response unaffected while carrying a residual stress. The chiral coupling enters at second order, through the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant, so that every dislocated material couples the modes as the Mooney--Rivlin solid with the same second- and third-order moduli. At third order, no new coupling arises; the modes interact through stiffness corrections involving the fourth-order modulus, which the dislocations further correct mode by mode.

title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
abstract: Solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion offers a compelling route to harvest sub-bandgap photons to increase the efficiency of photovoltaics, but low sensitizer doping required to suppress non-radiative aggregation quenching severely restricts light absorption. Here, we present a dual-resonator planar silver microcavity housing a thermally co-evaporated rubrene:palladium phthalocyanine (PdPC) active layer designed to simultaneously enhance triplet-sensitizer absorption and out-couple upconverted emission. By aligning a dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak at $32^\circ$, we achieve a 12-fold enhancement in absorptance at 665 nm. This absorption boost, combined with directional outcoupling through a second cavity mode, outweighs cavity-induced reabsorption losses to yield a 22-fold peak and 4.5-fold integrated enhancement in detected upconversion emission. Overall, this work highlights the potential of microcavity integration to substantially enhance solid-state upconversion performance across low-intensity optoelectronic applications.

title: Spectral signatures of spin textures and the emergence of a pseudogap
abstract: Periodic solids with strongly interacting electrons display phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories and the associated frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. We showcase this perspective by studying the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model. We find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet displays, in addition to stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy of the self-energy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such an intricate many-body state: the pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and the metallic interfaces, which echoes the role of spin-fluctuations identified by nonperturbative methods.

title: MIND: Instruction-Conditioned Incremental Grounding for Robots
abstract: Robots following persistent language instructions must decide which cached room judgments remain valid as their environment changes. We present MIND (Maintenance via INstruction-conditioned Dependencies), a framework for maintaining target-room decisions without re-evaluating every room after each event. A language model compiles each instruction into dependencies for semantic qualification and target selection. The controller intersects semantic dependencies with event footprints, refreshes affected judgments, and updates reachability and selection separately. For fixed deterministic evaluation, planning, and selection, conservative dependency and footprint coverage preserves the decisions of full recomputation. On 240 five-event ProcTHOR sequences with an exact benchmark predicate, MIND reduces mean semantic evaluations from 30.6 to 11.2 while preserving all 1,200 post-event decisions. Frozen-evaluator experiments with Phi-4 and Qwen3-14B also preserve all 1,200 decisions, without improving the evaluators' underlying task accuracy. In 32 closed-loop AI2-THOR episodes using exact-predicate qualification and metadata-derived footprints, MIND matches the final target decision of full recomputation in every episode. Unitree G1 experiments demonstrate target reuse and reselection across room transitions without additional semantic evaluations under MIND, and abstention after a barrier and an object removal at 4 evaluations against 15 to 18. Additional materials are available at https://mind-icra27.github.io/.

title: Atomic ironing for conformal interfaces in freestanding oxide nanomembranes
abstract: Atomically well-defined interfaces are essential for realizing functional interlayer coupling in stacked and twisted oxide heterostructures, yet transferred freestanding oxides can develop structural inhomogeneities, including local curvatures, interfacial voids, and incomplete contacts with substrates. Here, we demonstrate that these transfer-induced structural disorders and imperfections evolve substantially and can be suppressed by post-transfer thermal treatments, yielding bulk-like crystalline freestanding oxide nanomembranes. Using freestanding SrTiO3 membranes as a model system, we report a systematic understanding of the role of "atomic ironing" and the associated evolution of lattice mosaicity, interfacial roughness, and optical bandgap. We further demonstrate atomically bonded conformal interfaces in twisted SrTiO3 heterostructures, highlighting the importance of post-transfer thermal processes. These results establish a synthetic strategy to restore the structural integrity and intrinsic bulk-like functionality of freestanding oxide nanomembranes, enabling stacked, twisted, and heterogeneously integrated oxide architectures with atomically well-defined interfaces for emerging quantum functionalities.

title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
abstract: The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Reliability of Machine Learning Approaches Towards the Identification of Novel PI4KIIIβ Inhibitors
abstract: IntroductionThe type III Phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase (PI4KIIIβ) serves as a key host factor that mediates the replication of RNA viruses and is involved in essential membrane trafficking events. The development of PI4KIIIβ-specific inhibitors could give insights into the enzyme's function and contribute to the treatment of viral diseases. However, the molecular features that determine inhibitor activity and selectivity remain unclear.MethodsPI4KIIIβ inhibitors with reported biological activities (pIC50) were systematically analyzed using machine-learning methods.

title: Divergent Kinetics and Rate-Determining Steps for 1-Butene and 2-Butene Hydroformylation with a Bidentate Phosphoramidite Ligand: A Combined Experimental and Density Functional Theory Study
abstract: The hydroformylation of mixed butenes (1-butene and 2-butene) to n-valeraldehyde is an important industrial process, yet the distinct kinetic behaviors of the two isomers under identical catalytic conditions remain insufficiently understood. Herein, a comprehensive kinetic and mechanistic investigation of 1-butene and 2-butene was conducted using a robust, water- and air-stable, highly regioselective bidentate phosphoramidite ligand-modified rhodium catalyst in a homogeneous system.

title: Enantioselective Alcohol Oxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Unspecific Peroxygenases
abstract: The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.

title: AT1R-Selective Negative Allosteric Modulator Targeting the Epitope for Pathogenic Autoantibody Activation
abstract: A major therapeutic strategy for managing cardiovascular and renal diseases is the use of angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs). These drugs block both pathogenic and physiological signaling by the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) by preventing angiotensin II (AngII) binding to orthosteric pocket in transmembrane portion of AT1R. However, in many autoimmune diseases, AT1R activation is chronically driven by pathogenic autoantibody binding to a distinct extracellular surface located allosteric site.

title: Thermal stability and structural ordering of thick Co$_2$MnAl films grown on MgO and Si substrates
abstract: While most studies on Co$2$MnAl (CMA) focus on the ultrathin regime for spintronic junctions, applications scaling with magnetic volume--such as Anomalous Nernst Effect (ANE) energy harvesters, integrated power inductors, and magnetic MEMS--require significantly thicker films. In this work, 750 nm thick CMA films were grown on MgO (001) and Si substrates to establish a roadmap for their thermal integration. Structural analysis reveals that B2 ordering is optimized on MgO at 600 $^\circ$C, which is important for functional devices. In contrast, samples on Si substrates exhibit a disorder transition toward the A2 phase, closely linked to diffusion-driven degradation processes. Above 500 $^\circ$C, Si interdiffusion into the Heusler layer triggers the formation of interfacial silicides and Kirkendall voids, leading to microcracking, electrical resistivity jumps, and a final fully disordered A2 phase. Despite the Mn-poor stoichiometry (Co$2.25$Mn$0.7$Al$1.05$), the films maintain a robust saturation magnetization of ~600 emu/cm$^3$, consistent with recent theoretical models for off-stoichiometric Heusler alloys. These results define the processing windows for integrating thick CMA layers into multifunctional CMOS-compatible platforms.

title: Structural heterogeneity of uncrosslinked FtsH-HflKC assemblies includes variable FtsH occupancy and a distinct wild-type FtsH architecture
abstract: The AAA+ metalloprotease FtsH associates with HflK and HflC to form the megadalton FtsH-HflKC complex (FHC), which contributes to membrane-protein quality control in Escherichia coli. Recent structural studies have revealed asymmetric HflKC architectures and variable FtsH occupancy, contrasting with earlier crosslinked structures of a symmetric four-hexamer cage. Here, we analyzed wild-type, uncrosslinked FHC co-expressed from a single multicistronic plasmid and solubilized in lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG) using single-particle cryo-EM, SEC-SAXS, and biochemical activity assays. Two-dimensional classification identified HflKC-containing particles associated with one or two FtsH hexamers, together with a distinct population of isolated FtsH particles. Focused reconstruction of the FtsH cytosolic domain reached 5.32 angstrom resolution and provided a structural view of wild-type, uncrosslinked FtsH without stabilizing substitutions or an added nucleotide analogue. The reconstruction retained the characteristic stacked arrangement of the AAA+ and protease rings but showed a more laterally splayed AAA+ ring compared with the stabilized reference, while the protease ring remained broadly similar in overall envelope. A 9.63 angstrom HflKC consensus reconstruction and 3D variability analysis (3DVA) in C1, further revealed substantial conformational variability spanning open-like and more constricted scaffold geometries. SEC-SAXS of a selected later-eluting LMNG-solubilized fraction yielded a compact anisotropic envelope with an estimated Dmax of ~110-115 angstrom, although this species could not be assigned to a defined intact FHC stoichiometry. Under the conditions tested, the FHC preparation also showed lower apparent ATPase and proteolytic activities than isolated FtsH. Together, these findings highlight the compositional and conformational heterogeneity of uncrosslinked FHC and reveal a more laterally splayed AAA+ arrangement in wild-type FtsH compared with the stabilized reference structure.

title: A learning-to-rank framework for large-scale identification of unknown proteins from cryo-EM and cryo-ET maps
abstract: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) can yield density maps whose molecular identities are unknown. Predicted-structure databases enable proteome-scale searches, but distinguishing the correct candidates remains challenging, particularly for intermediate-resolution maps without clear side-chain features. We developed CryoAssign, an automated framework that combines large-scale structure matching with learning-to-rank prioritization. CryoAssign searches intact density maps without prior segmentation and integrates complementary measures of map-model agreement. On held-out benchmark maps, CryoAssign robustly prioritized the correct candidates. It also identified proteins or narrowed the set of candidates in previously unassigned cryo-EM maps and recovered multiple components from complex cryo-EM and cryo-ET maps. Controlled low-pass filtering showed generally robust recovery across a broad range of intermediate resolutions. CryoAssign provides a scalable approach for identifying proteins from cryo-EM and cryo-ET density maps.

title: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
abstract: Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions.

title: Nano-CeO2-Derived BaCeO3– x N y H z : A High-Purity Oxynitride-Hydride Support for Enhanced Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: Hetero-anion doping has emerged as an effective approach to modulate the physicochemical and catalytic properties of perovskite-type oxides. In this study, nanosized CeO2 synthesized by a continuous flow-type supercritical hydrothermal synthesis (SHS) process was employed as a precursor for a solid-state reaction with Ba(NH2)2, enabling the low-temperature synthesis of single-phase perovskite oxynitride–hydride BaCeO3–xNyHz (BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS) with a high surface area and abundant N3– and H– species.

title: Detection of Cervical Nodal Metastasis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Using Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy: Ex Vivo Diagnostic Modeling Study
abstract: BackgroundCervical nodal metastasis remains one of the strongest determinants of treatment planning and prognosis in oral squamous cell carcinoma. Histopathology remains the reference standard, but it does not provide immediate information at the point of surgical specimen assessment. Elastic scattering spectroscopy (ESS) offers rapid, label-free optical interrogation of tissue microstructure, and may support ex vivo nodal assessment.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of ESS combined with machine learning classification for ex vivo detection of cervical lymph node metastasis in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma.MethodsWe conducted a single-center observational ex vivo diagnostic modeling study in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma undergoing primary tumor resection and neck dissection. A total of 3 ESS spectra were acquired from each bivalved lymph node before routine histopathological processing. Internal validation used repeated nested 5-fold cross-validation grouped by patient, so every spectrum and lymph node from a patient remained in the same fold. All preprocessing, scaling, dimensionality reduction, within-model-family configuration, and hyperparameter tuning, probability calibration where required, and decision-threshold selection were restricted to training data within the nested validation process; comparisons between candidate model families were exploratory and were based on pooled patient-grouped out-of-fold predictions. Spectrum-level probabilities were aggregated within each lymph node, and histopathology was the reference standard.ResultsA total of 52 patients were assessed for eligibility, 45 were included, and 280 fresh lymph nodes were assessed by ESS; 96 were pathology positive, and 184 were pathology negative. Of 840 acquired spectra, 760 passed quality control. Of the 280 nodes, 274 retained at least 2 usable spectra and comprised the analytical cohort; 6 pathology-negative nodes yielded no analyzable node-level ESS result. The hybrid model was selected because it had the highest pooled patient-grouped out-of-fold node-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), with an internally validated, exploratory estimate of 0.966 (95% CI 0.929-0.988). The same out-of-fold predictions informed model-family selection and performance reporting; this estimate does not represent independent validation of a prospectively fixed final model. At the cross-validation-derived summary threshold, secondary descriptive operating characteristics were sensitivity 93.8% (95% CI 86.4%-97.6%), specificity 95.5% (95% CI 90.1%-98.3%), accuracy 94.9% (95% CI 90.4%-97.3%), positive predictive value 91.8% (95% CI 82.9%-96.3%), and negative predictive value 96.6% (95% CI 92.4%-98.8%). The Brier score was 0.063, with calibration-in-the-large of -0.03 and a calibration slope of 0.94. Patient-level sensitivity was 96% and specificity was 90%. Pathology-positive and pathology-negative nodes also showed differences across amplitude-related and shape-related spectral features.ConclusionsESS showed promising ex vivo discrimination of metastatic cervical lymph nodes in this single-center model-development and internal-validation study. The findings support further investigation of ESS as a potential pathology-triage adjunct rather than a replacement for histopathology.
